campaign: 2026-09-30: QR3, TPOT at the 95th percentile for one user, on the engine's serving plan (ctx 4096), planned against a dated memory snapshot

supersedes.why: its plans used memory_at_rest.json (2026-09-27); serve_pool.sh's gate refused the 14B plan at 01:28:56 (Pi 5 7,435 MiB available against 7,619 on file, margin 89 MiB). No server started; no per-token figure existed. Requirement, definitions, rules and predicted verdicts are copied from it verbatim.

requirement: HeteroServe_Proposal_EN.docx: 'TPOT P95 <= 500 ms (MVP) / <= 250 ms (Stretch)'; TPOT measured as decode streams tokens back to the client
instrument: testbed/scripts/qr3_tpot.py run --model <key> --ctx 4096 --mem testbed/dataset/memory_snapshot_20260930_013353.json --clocks locked --reqs 10 --n 128 --gen 128 (tag 'scored'): serve_pool.sh starts the plan; the model's sha256 is checked on its host first; one unscored warm-up (512-token prompt, 32 tokens), then 10 requests one after another, each its own 128-token prompt (GPL-3 from token 500 x i, then a question), 128 tokens each, greedy, ignore_eos, cache_prompt false, streamed with timings_per_token; get_throttled / temperature / MemAvailable on every board between requests; no memory probe during scored requests. The configs run in the order listed. Each config starts only once its host is below 50 C (Pi 5) or 57 C (Pi 4), waiting up to 10 min. The Jetson's clocks are locked for every config it serves in (run_pool.sh's commands: stored, locked, restored after), except the secondary config qwen3_14b_asfound, which leaves them to the governors (--clocks asfound --tag asfound).

definitions.tpot_sample: the gap between two consecutive tokens of one request (the first token is TTFT's): 127 samples a request, 1,270 a config. An SSE event carrying more than one token gives no sample for the gap it merges; merged events are counted and reported.
definitions.client: the laptop's time.perf_counter() at each SSE event's arrival: what a user on the router LAN sees. PRIMARY.
definitions.server: llama-server's timings.predicted_ms per token (stamped after sampling, us resolution); a sample only where predicted_n rises by exactly 1. Reported beside the primary, to separate the cluster from the delivery path.
definitions.p95: the 95th percentile of a config's pooled samples, by linear interpolation between order statistics (numpy's default, Hyndman-Fan type 7)
definitions.ci: 95 % CI of the pooled P95 by bootstrap over whole requests (10,000 resamples, seed 20260930), because tokens of one request are not independent
definitions.mean_tpot: the mean of the pooled samples

rules: QR3-MVP: a config meets the MVP if its pooled client P95 is <= 500 ms. It is reported as 'met' when the whole CI is <= 500, 'met on the point estimate' when only the P95 is, and 'not met' otherwise.
PRIMARY: the verdicts are taken on the client samples. If the server samples would give a different verdict, both are reported.
TAIL: QR3 is decided by the mean decode speed, not by jitter: every config's pooled client P95 is within 10 % above its mean TPOT (P95 / mean <= 1.10).
DELIVERY: the pooled client and server P95 of every config differ by less than 2 %.

ACCURACY: every config's server mean TPOT is within +-10 % of the predictor's decode figure for its plan (as the engine and serve_pool.sh use it, with no recurrent term). Expected to hold for the dense models; the 9B hybrid and the MoE carry the known biases in their notes, and are scored against the rule as written.
PLAN: the plan serve_pool.sh serves must be the registered one (its server args); a config served on another plan is reported and not scored.
COMPLETE: every scored request must return exactly 128 tokens; a config with a short request is reported, its full requests still scored.

predicted_verdicts.QR3-MVP: met only by qwen3moe (predicted mean 273.7 ms); the dense models and the 9B are predicted not to meet it (their predicted means already exceed 500 ms, except the 9B's plain 466.3, which its known bias puts above)

predicted.recur_term_note: information only: RECUR's host term, fitted on the Pi 5's own tg16 row of this model, so for this one-board plan it restates that row; ACCURACY uses the plain figure

qwen35_9b.note: a qwen35 hybrid: the registered rule TRANSFER (2026-09-28) found the predictor 5-14 % optimistic in decode for it, and RECUR2's decode term was not adopted, so the plain figure is expected to be low

qwen3moe.note: the MoE: its warm llama-bench decode on the ctx-80 plan (13/10/25) ran 290.0 ms against 263.3 predicted (-9.2 %)

qwen3_14b_asfound.note: SECONDARY: the qwen3_14b plan with the Jetson's clocks left to its governors (nvhost_podgov, schedutil), as serve_pool.sh serves interactively. The predictor has no term for a governor; its figure is the locked one, and ACCURACY is applied as written.
